one_line: Gond ruler of Garha-Katanga who forged a fortified Narmada–Satpura kingdom and patronised Sanskrit learning in the early 16th century.

appearance.age_look: Mid-40s, sturdy and broad-shouldered with a seasoned warrior’s build.
appearance.face: Oval face with a strong jaw, medium-brown central Indian complexion, slightly prominent nose, neatly trimmed moustache, faint stubble along the jaw, and calm, assessing eyes with a steady, dignified default expression.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair gathered into a low knot at the back of the head, front smoothed and parted slightly off-centre, wrapped with a narrow deep-red cloth band like a simple turban-strip, leaving the top of the head mostly visible.
appearance.costume: A knee-length, long-sleeved cotton angarkha in muted off‑white with a subtle block-printed border in dark maroon along the neckline and front wrap, tied on the right with visible cloth ties; over it a sleeveless quilted war-vest in dull forest-green with vertical stitching and slightly darker green piping; a broad, soft cotton sash in deep maroon wrapped twice around the waist and knotted on the left with its ends hanging to mid-thigh; straight, ankle-length trousers in earthy brown; sturdy dark-brown leather sandals with thong straps; simple jewelry limited to a pair of small bronze hoop earrings and a single bronze bangle on his left wrist, keeping the overall look functional and courtly rather than ostentatious.
appearance.signature: A slightly curved Talwar-like steel sword with a simple disc pommel and plain cross-guard, sheathed in a dark-brown leather scabbard with minimal brass fittings, worn at his left hip on a plain brown leather belt, often held in his left hand while his right carries a rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a thin cord to reflect his role as both warrior and patron of Sanskrit learning.

ref_desc: Sangram Shah is a mid-40s broad-shouldered Gond ruler with medium-brown skin, oval face, black hair in a low knot bound by a deep-red band, wearing an off-white angarkha, forest-green quilted vest, maroon sash, brown trousers, leather sandals, and carrying a simple curved sword with brown scabbard and a rolled palm-leaf manuscript.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Sangram Shah: a mid-40s, sturdy, broad-shouldered Gond king with medium-brown complexion, oval face, strong jaw, calm assessing eyes, and a neat moustache with light stubble; his thick black hair is pulled into a low knot at the back and wrapped with a narrow deep-red cloth band like a simple turban-strip, leaving most of the top of his head visible. He wears a knee-length, long-sleeved off-white cotton angarkha with a subtle dark maroon block-printed border along the neckline and front wrap, tied on the right with visible cloth ties, over which sits a sleeveless, vertically quilted war-vest in dull forest-green with slightly darker green piping. Around his waist is a broad deep maroon cotton sash wrapped twice and knotted on the left, its ends hanging to mid-thigh, over straight ankle-length earthy-brown trousers and dark-brown leather thong sandals. Add small bronze hoop earrings and a single bronze bangle on his left wrist for restrained courtly detail. At his left hip hangs a slightly curved steel sword with simple cross-guard and disc pommel in a dark-brown leather scabbard with minimal brass fittings on a plain brown leather belt, and in his other hand he holds a rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a thin cord, symbolising his combined roles as warrior and patron of Sanskrit learning; use a palette of off-white, forest green, deep maroon, earthy brown, and dark brown leather, and present front, side, and back views to clearly show the fixed hairstyle, garments, and weapons.
